security_audit.summary: All 97 static detections are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documentation links, CSS selectors, or expected migration-script behavior. The script changes the user-selected project and installs packages, but no evidence of prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The migration script edits files recursively and deletes the prior Tailwind configuration after backing it up.
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run mode, exclude dependency and version-control directories, and require confirmation before writes and package installation.

remediation.issue: The migration script installs packages using the latest version.
remediation.suggestion: Allow users to provide a reviewed version or lockfile-based installation path for reproducible migrations.

remediation.issue: Reference paths use both referenes and references naming.
remediation.suggestion: Correct and validate reference paths so users can locate all cited migration material.

content.value_statement: Tailwind CSS v4 changes configuration, utilities, and browser requirements. This skill provides structured guidance for migrations, component systems, and performance checks.
actual_capabilities: Plans v3 to v4 migrations with configuration and utility changes.
Explains CSS-first theme configuration with the @theme directive.
Designs reusable Tailwind v4 component class conventions.
Selects Tailwind integrations for Vite, PostCSS, or the CLI.
Identifies modern browser requirements for v4 CSS features.
Suggests build-time and stylesheet-size performance checks.
limitations: It does not execute migrations or validate a project automatically.
Verify Tailwind version details against official documentation before production changes.
Test visual output and browser compatibility in your own application.
The bundled migration script changes files and dependencies, so review it before running.

use_cases.title: Migrate an existing application
use_cases.description: Create a staged plan to move a Tailwind v3 application to v4 and verify important visual changes.

use_cases.title: Create a component foundation
use_cases.description: Define theme tokens, component classes, and modifier conventions for a consistent interface.

use_cases.title: Improve build workflows
use_cases.description: Review plugin choices and measurement steps for faster Tailwind development and production builds.

prompt_templates.title: Start a v4 project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up a small Tailwind CSS v4 project with CSS-first theme tokens. Explain each file and decision.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a v3 migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Tailwind v3 setup and create a safe Tailwind CSS v4 migration checklist. Include configuration, utility, and validation changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design shared components
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Tailwind CSS v4 component system for buttons, cards, and form fields. Define theme tokens, variants, and accessibility considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me investigate Tailwind CSS v4 build performance. Propose measurements, likely causes, plugin choices, and a verification plan.

output_examples.input: Plan a Tailwind v3 to v4 migration for a Vite application.
output: A mapping of configuration and utility updates.
A browser and visual regression validation plan.

output_examples.input: Create a shared theme for a product dashboard.
output: A token structure for color, spacing, and typography.
Guidance for documenting and testing the system.
A measurement plan for build and reload time.
Integration recommendations based on the build tool.
Steps to verify changes without visual regressions.

best_practices: Back up and review version control changes before a migration.
Keep theme tokens in one documented CSS-first source of truth.
Test responsive states, dark mode, and supported browsers after each migration phase.
anti_patterns: Do not delete existing configuration before confirming replacement theme tokens.
Do not apply broad utility replacements without reviewing affected components.
Do not assume modern CSS features work in unsupported browser versions.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Frontend developers and design system teams working with Tailwind CSS v4.

faq.question: Does it support Tailwind v3?
faq.answer: It focuses on v4 and can help plan a migration from v3.

faq.question: Can it run the migration for me?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and includes a script, but you should review and run changes yourself.

faq.question: Does it replace official documentation?
faq.answer: No. Confirm current APIs and release details in the official Tailwind documentation.

faq.question: What build tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers common v4 choices for Vite, PostCSS, and the Tailwind CLI.

faq.question: How should I validate a migration?
faq.answer: Use version control, build checks, visual regression tests, and browser compatibility testing.
